items.asks: Why the dataset fits the task
items.evidence: each real group is a held corpus of plain film or of fluoroscopy (README section 2), the families of the question's two kinds (PREREG.md section 1), the fluoroscopy family holding beside one mobile C-arm's spot frames DeepFluoro's vendor fluoroscopy of cadaver pelves, six specimens plus phantoms by the table's note, and a resin hip phantom (README section 2; data/domain_gap/groups.json); each group is capped by person so that a corpus with many images of few persons cannot outweigh the others (README section 2); the render groups render the same CTs and differ only by their recipe and engine (PREREG.md section 2), and README section 2.2 names six pairs, each meant to isolate one thing; README section 6 finds that the FLUX-edit pair measures the edit together with what else differs between its two sides, not the edit alone; what limits the fit was listed before the run, README section 5: the corpora differ in anatomy (cervical films, a hip phantom, cephalograms, abdomen), devices, eras and formats as well as in realism, and the renders follow their own pose profiles where the real spot frames are narrow and centred on the lumbar spine; and README section 6 records what the recorded runs do not support (CLAIM 40 quotes it)

the baselines are the real-against-real contrasts, every pair of tested real groups and pooled fluoroscopy against pooled film, the median AUC and median FD64 of a family's own real pairs being what each primary word and gap ratio is read against (PREREG.md sections 3 and 4), and the split-half nulls, where every test must find nothing (README section 1; CLAIM 32 quotes them); summary.txt carries such lines in the spaces flexray, imagenet; in the flexray space it reads "real-real auc median 1.00 min 0.97 max 1.00 over 36 pairs"; the families' own real pairs, among the tested real groups of summary.txt: fluoroscopy 1 pair, carmlspine_spots against deepfluoro; film 21 pairs; README section 6 finds that, with two real corpora themselves told apart almost perfectly, the word "closer than two real corpora" says nothing of realism

items.asks: Preprocessing fit on training data only
items.evidence: every classifier fits its scaler and PCA inside its own pipeline on the rows it is trained on: the C2ST's in each fold on the folds that hold none of the scored rows' persons, and the classifier that calls each synthetic group on the real rows alone (tools/domain_gap_stats.py, classifier, c2st and nearest_real), so no row shapes its own score; each image is windowed by its own percentiles, so decoding fits nothing across images (README section 3); the standardised features and first 64 components that the MMD, FD64, KID64, PRDC and the structure measures read are fit on every row of the reading without its labels, so they are the same under every permutation of a test's labels (tools/domain_gap.py at commit 6e908e6, space_head)

by person: every test's folds are grouped by person, so no person is on both sides of a split, and two render groups on one CT folder are read as a paired sample whose two views of a CT fall in one fold (tools/domain_gap.py at commit 6e908e6); in the 7 groups whose persons are their files (summary.txt, persons by file: fluorogen, aasce, nhanes2, csxa, kub_stonex, ieee_lateral, aariz) only files are held apart

every feature is computed from one image's pixels alone, by the encoders and the physics measures (tools/domain_gap.py, stage_features), and two steps before them keep file properties from telling corpora apart (README section 3): each image is cut to its centre square, so no pad's flat border marks a corpus of non-square images, and resized to 256 alike, so the resolution step is the same for every group; each is also windowed to its own percentiles, and the primary reading is invariant to inversion, so polarity alone separates nothing in it; what still tells corpora apart besides realism, their anatomy, devices, eras and formats (JPEG re-exports, 16-bit scans, DICOM) among them, was listed before the run in README section 5

items.asks: Uncertainty and how it was computed
items.evidence: summary.txt: 35 AUCs with an interval, 34 with a C2ST permutation p, 34 MMD permutation p and 6 Benjamini-Hochberg q; each interval the 95 percent percentile interval of a person-cluster bootstrap of 1,000 draws, the C2ST's p from 100 permutations and the MMD's from 1,000, all by person, and the q by Benjamini-Hochberg within a space, the MMD's over its contrasts and its split-half nulls as PREREG.md section 3 says, the worded pairs' q over the contrasts alone on their verdict lines (DEVIATIONS.md, item 11) (tools/domain_gap.py at commit 6e908e6 and tools/domain_gap_stats.py, README section 4)

the C2ST's 100 permutations, run against each family and in the replication pairs, and the MMD's 1,000 relabel the rows by person, every row of a person moving together, so each p holds under the null that persons are exchangeable between the two sets; where both sides hold the same persons, as two render groups on one CT folder do, the two worded replication pairs among them, the sample is paired: each person's two sides are swapped between the sets or left, so the p holds under the null that a person's two sides are exchangeable (tools/domain_gap_stats.py, twin_swaps; tools/domain_gap.py, contrast and Frame.twins), and the bootstrap draws a person with both its sides; the AUC's 95 percent interval is a person-cluster bootstrap that holds the scores of each fold's trained classifiers fixed and so leaves out the variance of fitting them, which on Gaussian clouds of one law ran about two-thirds as wide as the AUC's spread and covered 0.5 in 15 of 20 (tools/domain_gap_stats.py, auc_with_interval); DEVIATIONS.md item 8 calls it too narrow for a few dozen persons and flags a split-half null by its MMD instead, while the primary words and the replication word read its lower bound (PREREG.md section 4); Benjamini-Hochberg runs over a space's MMD p-values and over its C2ST permutation p-values (PREREG.md section 3; CLAIM 29 says which family this run's MMD q took), and no file of the study states the dependence among those p-values under which it controls the false-discovery rate; README section 6 finds DeepFluoro's persons are DICOM patient ids over six specimens and two phantoms, so its p-values and intervals are narrower than they should be, and that the paired bootstrap counts each CT's twin comparisons about twice
